s1.syndrome_frame: Acute vision loss in one eye with optic disc swelling and retinal vascular occlusion in a patient undergoing immunotherapy
salient_findings: Sudden vision loss in the right eye
Mild swelling of the optic disc
Occlusion of the superior branch artery
key_facts: Patient is a woman in her 40s
Undergoing treatment with systemic steroids, durvalumab, and bevacizumab
Initial visual acuity of 20/25 OU
Right eye showed full visual field
Mild swelling of the optic disc
Peripapillary retinal hemorrhages
Occlusion of the superior branch artery
Combined occlusion of the central retinal artery and vein
Vitreous biopsy showed hypercellular sample with astrocytic neoplasm
Immunohistochemistry positive for glial fibrillary acid protein and mutant IDH-1 protein

shortlist.label: Glioblastoma
shortlist.why_kept: Vitreous biopsy showed hypercellular sample with astrocytic neoplasm, and immunohistochemistry was positive for glial fibrillary acid protein and mutant IDH-1 protein

shortlist.label: Bevacizumab-Associated Optic Neuropathy
shortlist.why_kept: Patient is undergoing treatment with bevacizumab, which is known to cause optic neuropathy

shortlist.label: Durvalumab-Associated Optic Neuropathy
shortlist.why_kept: Patient is undergoing treatment with durvalumab, which is known to cause optic neuropathy

shortlist.label: Central Retinal Artery Occlusion
shortlist.why_kept: Combined occlusion of the central retinal artery and vein, and peripapillary retinal hemorrhages

shortlist.label: Optic Disc Edema
shortlist.why_kept: Mild swelling of the optic disc and marked swelling after vision loss

raw.rationale: The patient's vision loss and optic disc swelling occurred while undergoing treatment with bevacizumab, a known risk factor for optic neuropathy. The presence of peripapillary retinal hemorrhages and occlusion of the superior branch artery also supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Glioblastoma
rejected.why: Although the vitreous biopsy showed an astrocytic neoplasm, the clinical presentation and imaging studies do not support a primary diagnosis of glioblastoma.

rejected.label: Durvalumab-Associated Optic Neuropathy
rejected.why: While durvalumab is an immunotherapy agent that can cause optic neuropathy, the temporal relationship between bevacizumab administration and vision loss makes bevacizumab a more likely culprit.

rejected.label: Central Retinal Artery Occlusion
rejected.why: This is a secondary complication that occurred after the initial vision loss, rather than the primary cause of the patient's symptoms.

rejected.label: Optic Disc Edema
rejected.why: This is a nonspecific finding that does not fully explain the patient's vision loss and other clinical features.

gold: Glioblastoma (World Health Organization grade IV) with optic nerve invasion and intraocular extension
